title: Lights Out
paragraphs: One of radio's landmark horror anthologies, using sound and surreal situations to explore ghosts, monsters, murder, the supernatural, and psychological terror in stories associated especially with Wyllis Cooper and Arch Oboler.
Landmark horror anthology created by Wyllis Cooper and later led by Arch Oboler. Three later-dated GRH audio pairs contain earlier recordings despite metadata for distinct later broadcasts.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Wyllis Cooper national NBC era (April 18, 1935 to June 3, 1936) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Arch Oboler NBC era (June 10, 1936 to August 16, 1939) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], CBS sponsored revival (October 6, 1942 to September 28, 1943) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], and NBC summer revival (1945-07 to 1945-09) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Arch Oboler (host, writer, and director), Frank Martin (commercial spokesman and announcer), Mercedes McCambridge (performer), Albert Crews (director and producer), Wyllis Cooper (writer and director), Boris Aplon (performer), and Lou Merrill (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].

The stories often return to death, burial and confinement, murder and violent death, monsters and inhuman creatures, curses, occult forces and ritual, dangerous science and experiments, and ghosts and hauntings.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Experimental radio horror and sound design, Wyllis Cooper to Arch Oboler creative transition, 1942-43 CBS revival and script reproduction, and Lights Out as a cross-media horror property.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|richard-diamond-private-detective|Richard Diamond, Private Detective]].

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to CBS Radio Network, NBC Radio Network, and Armed Forces Radio and Television Service.

The stories often return to death, burial and confinement, murder and violent death, monsters and inhuman creatures, curses, occult forces and ritual, dangerous science and experiments, and ghosts and hauntings.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Experimental radio horror and sound design, Wyllis Cooper to Arch Oboler creative transition, 1942-43 CBS revival and script reproduction, and Lights Out as a cross-media horror property.
